text:
Morgan: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A. Folks asked for a crisp playbook: how do we keep our serving edge vs hyperscalers and niche inference vendors? Looking for practical steps, not philosophical answers.
Asha: High level: make it expensive for customers to leave. That means predictable costs, battle-tested ops, and integrations that are painful to rewire.
Riley: Can we define the one-page copy for sales/marketing? Something that isn't just "fast" but says exactly what to expect.
Priya: Field notes: 3 value props that win deals: SLA-backed latency bands, clear unit-cost math, and a validated migration path from their current endpoints.
Noor: Engineering POV: top technical hooks are: prefix caching, KV cache warmup, and runtime kernels tuned per model family. Those translate to fewer tokens billed and lower p95.
Diego: On migrate path: we should publish a migration checklist and a small open-source adapter for common vendor API shapes. That lowers friction.
Sam: For product signals, what should we instrument this quarter to tell if messaging is working? Need things dashboards can show by EOW.
Morgan: Start with three easy metrics: 1) # of accounts completing Dedicated evaluation (30d), 2) median 95th latency for new Dedicated customers, 3) % of support tickets referencing "cost surprise".
Asha: Ops deliverables for 90 days: 1) benchmark suite with 3 customer profiles (chat, summarize, embeddings); 2) Dedicated onboarding runbook + 1-pager for Legal; 3) public perf FAQ.
Liam: I'll own the competitor digest. Weekly email + single Notion table. Want perf columns and licensing notes.
Priya: I'll feed Liam deal-level snippets (anonymized) and contract clauses that mattered in recent wins.
Riley: Messaging angle: two landing pages. "Predictable unit economics" for enterprises and "fast iteration, low-cost dev loop" for startups. Keep both simple.
Noor: Quick engineering caveat: Optimize's quant suggestions need a labeled rollback plan. Suggestion -> A/B -> quality gate. Don't auto-apply at first.
Diego: Agree. Plan for Console: suggestions are draft state until a customer opts in. Also add a "replay" button to re-run evals against saved prompts.
Morgan: Nice. Who takes the action items?
Asha: I'll draft the 90-day epic and benchmarks.
Liam: I will ship the competitor digest starting next Monday.
Priya: I'll hand off the win/loss notes and contract excerpts.
Sam: I'll add the three metrics to the product dashboard and share a lightweight chart template.
InfraBot: Note uploaded: all-hands Q&A summary + draft epic -> https://confluence.redwood/ah/1726723345.
Morgan: Thanks all. Follow-up sync scheduled in two weeks. If anyone wants to join the benchmark working group ping me or Asha. :calendar:
